taxonomyNote: NatureServe places North American treefrogs in Dryophytes (Duellman et al. 2016); ADW and the batch list use Hyla. NatureServe name: Dryophytes femoralis.
fieldMarks: About 4-4.5 cm; reddish brown to gray-green with dark blotches and sometimes a dark band through the eye and eardrum.
Orange to silver spots or blotches on the rear of the thighs.
Breeding male has a dark throat.
Call is a raspy staccato, like Morse code or a cicada.
behavior: Mostly arboreal, perching from low shrubs to treetops; most active at night in spring through fall.
Calls from vegetation up to about 3 m above water, often as rain approaches.
Hides in or under rotting logs, stumps or snags in dry or cold weather; larvae metamorphose in 7-10 weeks.
habitat: Longleaf pine-wiregrass flatwoods and savannas and pine-turkey oak sandhills near bogs or ponds; occasionally hardwood forests and swamps.
range: Atlantic and Gulf Coastal Plains from southern Virginia to eastern Louisiana and south to southern Florida. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Squirrel treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Light stripe on the upper jaw and no orange spots on the thighs.
